attestation: Use RSA_generate_key_ex() As of OpenSSL 0.9.8, RSA_generate_key() is deprecated in favor of RSA_generate_key_ex(). RSA_generate_key_ex() requires passing in a BIGNUM* exponent, for which we use a crypto::ScopedBIGNUM. The end result is no functional change, but better alignment for openssl 1.1 migration and/or boringssl. chaps: Update for OpenSSL 1.1 OpenSSL 1.1 has made significant non-backwards compatible changes to its API as outlined in: https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/OpenSSL_1.1.0_Changes Among other things that have changed are new()/free() semantics for the various CTX structs, which are also conveniently wrapped in libchrome Scoped* objects. This allows us to simplify and better manage the context lifecycles. Note: there is one small behavior change buried in this CL. RSA_set0_key() requires that both n & e be non-null. Thus, in session_impl.c::CreateRSAKeyFromObject, when creating a private RSA key, we must now also always parse out the PUBLIC exponent such that it can be set along with the modulus and private exponent. power: deal with the energy counter wrap around cases Under the hood, the energy status MSR wraps around in case of: - Integer overflow as energy increasing monotonically - System in-and-out suspend-to-RAM (S3 but not S0ix) In both cases, the program generates an enormously large energy delta leading a large power in Watts. To tackle such odd, using the max_energy_range_uj node which is the interface exposed by the powercap driver, it indicates the maximum energy counting, we detect integer overflow case, drop the sample with very large power consumption. Notice that there is one corner case not covering by this patch. Namely, a very large polling interval along with counter wraps around passing the pre-snapshot energy reading, the calculated energy delta will be very small, which generates an enormously small average power against the other power domains; For example, we can setup an average 20 Watts system in psys domain by menas of WebGL aquarium sample, the particular energy counter shall overflow within 4 hours theoretically, in such case if we execute the utility with a large polling interval over 4 hours, it leads an odd causes the psys average power smaller than the the package power. BACKPORT: KVM: race-free exit from KVM_RUN without POSIX signals The purpose of the KVM_SET_SIGNAL_MASK API is to let userspace "kick" a VCPU out of KVM_RUN through a POSIX signal. A signal is attached to a dummy signal handler; by blocking the signal outside KVM_RUN and unblocking it inside, this possible race is closed: VCPU thread service thread -------------------------------------------------------------- check flag set flag raise signal (signal handler does nothing) KVM_RUN However, one issue with KVM_SET_SIGNAL_MASK is that it has to take tsk->sighand->siglock on every KVM_RUN. This lock is often on a remote NUMA node, because it is on the node of a thread's creator. Taking this lock can be very expensive if there are many userspace exits (as is the case for SMP Windows VMs without Hyper-V reference time counter). As an alternative, we can put the flag directly in kvm_run so that KVM can see it: VCPU thread service thread -------------------------------------------------------------- raise signal signal handler set run->immediate_exit KVM_RUN check run->immediate_exit Reviewed-by: Radim Krčmář <rkrcmar@redhat.com> Reviewed-by: David Hildenbrand <david@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com> BUG=None TEST=Built. power_status: deal with RAPL energy wrap around case Current implementation is assuming the powercap sysfs energy counter increases monotonically, unfortunately this is wrong because it would wrap around periodically when it reaches the max capacity, in such case, current autotest will calculate the energy delta in a negative number, this happens in every power domain. To tackle this odd, we detect the counter wrap around, use the interface of max energy to calculate the energy delta. cryptohome: Move unmount operations to the MountHelper class. With all mount operations moved to the helper, this CL now moves all unmount operations to the helper as well. Having both mount and unmount operations in the helper is a prerequisite to moving these operations out of process and eventually to carry them out in a non-root mount namespace. While the actual unmount operations and other clean-up functionality got moved to the MountHelper class, this functionality is still triggered in and by the Mount class. When moving the functionality out of process, more of the unmount and clean-up logic will be triggered by the MountHelper class. This CL also removes the RememberMount/RememberBind functions, which were kept around for testing in a previous CL. BUG=chromium:985492 TEST=Unit tests pass.
